Use a Tier 2 change focused on model_design and training_evaluation: replace score-dependent hard-negative mining with uniformly sampled negatives in the existing sampled-softmax objective. The latest trial achieved macro validation HR@10 of 0.4775, below the reported 0.5037 best and 0.505 baseline. This motivates testing whether the negative-selection objective is limiting generalization before adding further architectural complexity.

Draw one shared pool of 256 distinct, uniformly sampled nonzero item IDs per batch, then mask each user's complete training history and positive target. Remove the 1,024-item mining pool and selection of the 64 highest-scoring negatives; compute cross-entropy directly against all eligible sampled negatives. Uniform sampling better matches the benchmark's uniformly sampled distractors, while reducing emphasis on high-scoring unobserved items that may represent plausible preferences. Keep the gated SASRec architecture, transition weighting, augmentation, optimizer, and training schedule unchanged so this experiment isolates negative selection.

Retain all four categories, unchanged supplied splits, training seed 42, and fixed validation users and candidates with evaluation seed 42. Select exactly one checkpoint per category by validation HR@10, and ensure the predictor writer reconstructs that same trained network with identical history packing and scoring. Report the macro-average HR@10 across all four categories and compare it with the supplied references; leave hidden test inference to the host evaluator.
